# Flow 1: a freelancer registers a project that uses git and has Orbiter find it.
#
# Real bundled integrations (installed by vessel init), the real git, and a PATH holding
# exactly one git. A client answers Orbiter's prompts, as a GUI would.

step set up the vessel: install the bundled integrations
exec orbiter --output json vessel init -y
stdout '"installed":[1-9][0-9]*'

step register the universe: a galaxy, a planet in it, and a git resource attached to the planet
exec orbiter --output json galaxy add acme
exec orbiter --output json planet add api --galaxy acme
exec orbiter --output json resource add git --role tool --brand git
exec orbiter --output json attach git api

step survey the planet: everything is registered and nothing is verified yet
exec orbiter survey api -v
stdout 'tool/git'
stdout 'unverified'

step calibrate: the real git integration asks the Captain before it runs git
# The client answers both questions about the command, each a txn-tagged prompt:
# "git wants to run: git --version", then "Always allow this exact command?".
client -- calibrate api
stdout '"op":"CONFIRM"'
stdout '"message":"git wants to run: git --version"'
stdout '"message":"Always allow this exact command for \\"git\\"'
finding the approval names the bare command (git --version), not a resolved binary path: it is asked before FIND has run (roadmap Phase 3)

step the run cannot go on until git is found: it asks the client for discovery
stdout '"status":"needs_discovery"'
stdout '"op":"FIND_BINARY","key":"git"'
capture SESSION '"session":"([0-9a-z]+)"'
capture TXN '"txn":"([0-9a-z]+)","op":"FIND_BINARY"'

step the client plays the shell: Orbiter does not know this shell, so it asks the shell integrations
# Not a stub. This is the user's own shell (the flow's $FLOW_SHELL, the host login shell, zsh on
# a Mac) loading its profile line. Orbiter has no record of a shell yet, so it goes out to the
# registered shell integrations, one of them answers that this environment is its own, and
# Orbiter records that and hands back that integration's hook. Orbiter names no shell anywhere.
exec $FLOW_SHELL -c 'eval "$(orbiter shell init)"; FIND_BINARY "$TXN" git'
stderr 'registered .* as this vessel.s shell'

step Orbiter now has the shell on record
exec orbiter --output json survey vessel -v
stdout '"role":"shell"'

step the next terminal needs no detection: Orbiter uses its own record
exec $FLOW_SHELL -c 'orbiter shell init > /dev/null'
! stderr 'registered'

step continue the run: uplink records the path and calibrates again
client -- uplink --session=$SESSION
stdout '"type":"result"'
stdout '"action":"healthy"'
stdout '"binary_path":"[^"]*/bin/git"'

step the recorded path is in the star chart, in the form that travels between machines
exec orbiter --output json survey api -v
stdout '"binaries":\{"git":"[^"]*/bin/git"\}'

step a later scan finds git healthy and needs nothing more from the Captain
client -- scan api
stdout '"status":"healthy"'
stdout '"present":true'
! stdout '"status":"needs_discovery"'
